label: Bible Study
prompt: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the _____.
verse: And the earth was without form, and void; and darkness was upon the face of the deep. And the Spirit of God moved upon the face of the waters.
note: Before day one's light switch, the scene is dark, formless, and wet — with the Spirit hovering over it all.

label: Warm-Up Word
prompt: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without _____:
verse: Which doeth great things and unsearchable; marvellous things without number:
note: Eliphaz describes God's works as marvellous things without number — nobody can count that high.

label: Sunday School
prompt: And when she knew Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for _____, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.
verse: And when she knew Peter's voice, she opened not the gate for gladness, but ran in, and told how Peter stood before the gate.
note: Rhoda was so glad to hear Peter's voice that she ran to tell everyone — and left him standing at the gate.

label: Deep Water
prompt: Thou shalt not curse the deaf, nor put a _____ before the blind, but shalt fear thy God: I am the LORD.
verse: Thou shalt not curse the deaf, nor put a stumblingblock before the blind, but shalt fear thy God: I am the LORD.
note: Don't trip the blind or curse the deaf: the Law protects even people who'd never know who did it.

label: Don't Play With Me
prompt: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a _____ were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
verse: But whoso shall offend one of these little ones which believe in me, it were better for him that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and that he were drowned in the depth of the sea.
note: Jesus' fierce protectiveness of little ones: better a 'millstone' round the neck than to make one of them stumble.
